written.headline: Goldman Sachs and Apollo seek investors for up to $500 M slices of SpaceX’s $40 B chip financing
written.summary: Goldman Sachs and Apollo are approaching Wall Street investors to sell portions of SpaceX’s roughly $40 billion GPU debt financing, with some investors asked to buy up to $500 million before the syndication process begins. The financing, structured to stay off SpaceX’s balance sheet, is the largest GPU debt arrangement on record.

written.headline: AI‑focused PACs spent $72 million on 2026 midterms, many backed candidates lost
written.summary: AI‑aligned political action committees spent roughly $72 million on the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, with several high‑profile candidates they supported, such as South Carolina Senate hopeful Darline Graham, losing their races. The spending produced mixed outcomes, and a large share of the money went to losing candidates or efforts to defeat winners.

written.headline: Google will cut search access for schools that reject its AI tools
written.summary: Google announced that K‑12 accounts will lose Google Search unless administrators enable its Gemini AI suite, effectively forcing schools to adopt AI to retain search. The policy, set to take effect next year, has drawn criticism from educators and officials.

written.headline: OpenAI launches Images 2.6 with faster generation and GIF creation
written.summary: OpenAI announced Images 2.6, which adds faster image generation, GIF creation, more precise editing, and new API controls across ChatGPT, Codex and the API.
